title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: In Niger in 2025, ICSP improved humanitarian response by enabling rapid, community‑led action during recurrent flooding, market shocks and seasonal food insecurity. Community observatories, Village Development Committees and Disaster Preparedness Committees played a growing role in risk detection, early alerting and mobilisation of households for protective measures. Partnerships with local authorities and technical services strengthened preparedness and anticipation capacity, leading to quicker activation of contingency actions, including targeted cash support during flood events. These coordinated, locally anchored systems provided more predictable and timely humanitarian readiness across high‑risk communes.. Crisis anticipation in Niger relies on close collaboration between communities and government structures. ICSP prioritises partnerships with local authorities and technical services to strengthen preparedness systems, improve early‑warning coordination and enable timely, organised responses to recurrent floods and food‑security shocks.
